title: NADH-linked microtiter plate-based assay for measuring Rubisco activity
author: Cristina Rodrigues Gabriel Sales
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgajjscn
materials: REAGENTS & SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE BEFOREHAND Powder chemical stocks stored at -20°C: let warm up to room temperature on desiccant before opening container. Expensive chemicals purchased in very small amounts (mg), for which concentration in assay is not critical (e.g. in excess): trust quantity stated by the supplier and add ultrapure H 2 O / solvent to container for final concentration (e.g. 2,3-dPGA). Protein and substrate solutions should typically be stored at -80°C. Freeze proteins in LN 2 before storing at -80°C. Store in small aliquots to prevent multiple freeze-thaw cycles. If using in consecutive days, protein solutions can be kept at 4°C. Buffers and solutions will last longer if filtered through 0.22 µm membrane.

SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE JUST BEFORE USE Prepared with reagents/solutions described in step 1.

START Thaw the frozen solutions that will be used in the day. Prepare CO 2 -free ultrapure H 2 O by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/100 mL). Turn on the microplate reader and set up for the temperature that Rubisco activity will be performed, select kinetic protocol at 340 nm. The temperature to be used for the Rubisco activity measurement depends on the experiment goals. Typical measurement temperatures are 25 °C (standard) and 30 °C , depending on the species. Assays can be performed at a range of temperatures, however high temperatures might lead to evaporation of the assay mix and, since rates will be faster, the assay might become less sensitive. Turn on the centrifuge and set to 4 °C . Collect samples from -80 °C into liquid nitrogen container. Prepare the complete extraction buffer (from step 3.1) and the complete assay buffer (from step 3.2) and keep it On ice .

steps.title: Prepare Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following stock reagents and store as indicated:

substeps.instruction: Basic extraction buffer (1x): 50 mM Bicine-NaOH pH 8.2, 20 mM MgCl2.6H2O, 1 mM EDTA, 2 mM Benzamidine, 5 mM ε-Aminocaproic acid. Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH, degas by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/10 mL), and add 50 mM 2-Mercaptoethanol. Store at -20 °C in aliquots (e.g., 50 mL Falcon tubes).
1 M DTT: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O. Store at 4 °C.
100 mM PMSF: Dissolve in ethanol 99%. Store at 4 °C.
20 mM RuBP (≥99% purity): Store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Complete Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following components on ice to create the complete extraction buffer:

substeps.instruction: Basic extraction buffer (1x)
10 mM DTT
1 mM PMSF
1% (v/v) Plant protease inhibitor cocktail

steps.title: Prepare Complete Assay Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the assay buffer and NADH solution, keeping them on ice and wrapped in aluminum foil due to NADH light sensitivity.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the basic assay buffer and NADH aliquots on ice.
Mix the required volumes of assay buffer and NADH together (Example for 140 wells: 8344 µL assay buffer without NADH and 799.4 µL NADH).

steps.title: Set Up Microtiter Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the 96-well microtiter plate before starting the extraction process:

substeps.instruction: Pipette 129.7 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into the blank well (singlet).
Pipette 123.7 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into 6 sample wells (triplicates for initial activity, triplicates for total activity).
Add 65.3 µL of complete assay buffer to all wells.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down 5 times while stirring.
Add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP to the 3 wells designated for initial Rubisco activity.
Cover the plate to protect from light.

steps.title: Extract Plant Sample
steps.instruction: Perform rapid extraction to prevent Rubisco deactivation, ensuring the process takes no more than 1 minute.

substeps.instruction: Add complete extraction buffer to an ice-cold mortar.
Add a sample from liquid nitrogen to the mortar and grind thoroughly for 30 to 60 seconds.
Collect homogenate into an ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 minute at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant into a new ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Perform Rubisco Activity Assay
steps.instruction: Measure the NADH-linked activity by monitoring absorbance at 340 nm at 30 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL of sample supernatant to the 'total activity' wells first, then to the 'initial activity' wells, mixing by pipetting up and down 10 times while stirring.
Immediately place the plate in the reader and monitor absorbance at 340 nm.
Incubate the 'total activity' wells for 3 minutes at 30 °C to allow carbamylation.
After 3 minutes, pause the reading and add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP to the 'total activity' wells.
Resume monitoring absorbance until the reaction reaches a plateau.

steps.title: Calculate Rubisco Activity
steps.instruction: Determine the rate of RuBP consumption and activity based on the absorbance slope.

substeps.instruction: Calculate RuBP consumption (μmol s-1) using the formula: (Slope × Volume) / (6.22 × 2 × Pathlength), where Volume = 0.2 mL and 6.22 is the NADH extinction coefficient.
Calculate initial (Vi) or total (Vt) activity on a leaf area basis (µmol m-2 s-1): (RuBP consumption × Extraction volume in mL) / (Leaf area in m2 × Aliquot volume in mL).
Alternatively, calculate activity on a protein basis (μmol min-1 mg-1): (RuBP consumption × 60) / (Protein content in mg mL-1 × Aliquot volume in mL).
Calculate Activation State (AS, %): 100 × Vi / Vt.
